newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli, Omani banks establish ties.
newsitem.headline: Israeli, Omani banks establish ties.

text.p: Bank Hapoalim and Bank Muscat Al Ahli Al Omani of Oman have signed an agreement setting up formal banking ties, the Israeli bank said on Tuesday.
Hapoalim said that as far it knows this was the first such agreement between an Israeli and an Omani bank.
Officials at Hapoalim, Israel's biggest bank, said this was the opening of a door that would enable the start of trade and joint ventures between companies in the two countries.
Bank Muscat is the second biggest bank in Oman, Hapoalim said.
Israeli banks have formal accords with counterparts in other Arab countries, including Egypt, Jordan, Morocco and Tunisia.
Oman and Qatar have forged ahead of other Gulf states in establishing economic ties with Israel but have stopped short of full diplomatic relations.

In recent weeks, relations between Qatar and the Jewish state have cooled in the wake of fighting between Palestinians and Israelis that killed more than 70 people and cast doubts on the Middle East peace process.
But Oman's minister of state for foreign affairs said last week it was in the interest of Arab states to have links with Israel, which would then be convinced of the importance of peace.
